//: Spoken names are DATA, not logic. Nothing in the runtime or the skills knows that 'kimi' or 'sol' means anything: `resolve` matches a phrase against these lists. Adding a model, a backend, or another way of saying one, is an edit to this file and nothing else. Speed words (fast, quick, cheap, standard, full) are handled by resolve and are not listed here, so 'fast kimi' needs no entry of its own.
//backends: Two ways to actually run a model. `opencode` drives a local OpenCode server, which is how the non-OpenAI models are reachable. `codex` shells out to the Codex CLI, which runs OpenAI models on the ChatGPT sign-in rather than through a paid API key. Each alias names the backend it should use by default, and saying a backend word out loud overrides it: 'opencode sol' forces the OpenCode path. A backend also carries runsOn: which execution path it uses, which is not always itself. openrouter runsOn opencode, because OpenRouter is a provider reached through the same local server rather than a second way of running a job. Saying "openrouter" therefore swaps the provider and changes nothing else: same server, same agent config, same permission policy. Without this an alias could only have one provider per backend, and picking the other one meant editing the user's config by hand.

codex.description: The Codex CLI (codex exec) on your ChatGPT sign-in.

openrouter.description: OpenRouter, reached through the same local OpenCode server.

glm.//: Both tiers point at the same model on purpose. GLM has exactly one routed model, so 'glm' and 'fast glm' are the same request and there is no substitution worth reporting. 5.2 and plain 5.3 are retired above, not merely absent.

sol.//: Replaced gpt-5.6-sol. The 5.6 names are retired above rather than pointed here, because saying "gpt 5.6 sol" and getting a different model is the substitution this table exists to prevent. Written as pending ids on both backends, the way astra started: OpenCode lists opencode/gpt-6-sol, while Codex answers a ChatGPT-account request for gpt-6-sol with a 400. astra.description: GPT-6 Astra, the GPT-6 model that is live today. Runs through Codex on the ChatGPT sign-in; say opencode to run it on the API key instead.
astra.//backend: Live on both backends: the Codex model cache lists gpt-6-astra and a real `codex exec -m gpt-6-astra` completes, and OpenCode lists opencode/gpt-6-astra. Codex stays the default because it bills the ChatGPT sign-in rather than a metered key. It is still written as a reserved alias with pending ids, so each backend is used only while it actually lists the model. Bare "gpt 6" no longer means astra: GPT-6 is three models now, and that phrase is retired above so it asks which one.
astra.//pendingBackends: Candidate ids per backend, tried in order, promoted to real routes only when that backend actually offers one. So the day GPT-6 lands, 'have astra do X' works with no edit to this file, and until then astra refuses rather than guessing.
